key_insight: An optimized disturbance reveals the route from a turbulent puff’s splitting seed through an edge state to successful splitting, despite chaotic fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: Understanding how turbulent puffs proliferate could inform prediction and control of laminar–turbulent transition in pipe flows.
method: Apply nonlinear nonmodal optimization to a reduced-order model to identify a splitting seed.
Trace the seed-to-edge-to-splitting pathway in full Navier–Stokes dynamics.
Use an optimized splitting-progress coordinate to dynamically align chaotic realizations for ensemble averaging.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a splitting seed with strong velocity inflection and an energy threshold that scales as a power law with Reynolds number.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the validated Reynolds-number range or quantitative accuracy of the reduced-order predictions.
paper_title: An Optimal Seed Reveals the Dynamical Route to Spontaneous Splitting of Turbulent Puffs
